plainLanguageExplanation: A product is the new substance that a chemical reaction creates. When hydrogen and oxygen react, they combine into water — the water is the product. In a chemical equation, products are always written on the RIGHT side of the arrow: hydrogen + oxygen → water. The arrow means 'reacts to make,' and everything after it is a product. Products are genuinely new substances. The wood you burn, the carbon dioxide and ash that result — those are products. The cake you bake from flour and eggs — that is a product. And here is the crucial rule that connects products to reactants: the product's atoms are exactly the reactant's atoms, just rearranged. The same atoms that went into the reaction come out in the product — nothing is created or destroyed, only reconnected. That is why mass is conserved: the weight of the products exactly equals the weight of the reactants. Products are the other half of every reaction — the new thing that appears on the right of the arrow.

whyItMatters: Products are the outcome of every chemical change — the new substances that appear around you constantly, from the bread in your oven to the rust on a bike. Understanding products, and that their atoms come from the reactants, is central to reading equations and the law of conservation of mass.
didYouKnow: The carbon dioxide you exhale is a product — its carbon atoms came from the food you ate, and its oxygen from the air you breathed. You are breathing out rearranged dinner.
compareReason: Product and reactant are the two ends of every reaction — comparing the dish with the ingredients makes the whole reaction concept concrete.
